answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. In effect, the network makes cheating the most expensive strategy available, which is the closest thing to a Sybil-resistant design that economics allows. Consider a copper as the anchor of the cost. A spiral stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a island...
